Three weeks walking the Camino

The first morning, my feet already hated me. By the third day I had stopped counting kilometres and started counting cafés.

Every village had the same rhythm: bells, bread, a dog that followed you to the edge of town and then turned back.

You don't walk the road. The road walks you.

What I packed, and what I threw away

Two shirts, one book, far too many socks. The book stayed in a hostel in Burgos for the next person.

By the end I could tell the time from the colour of the sky, which is a skill I have since lost completely.
